## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: indicators, placards, renewal and amendments
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical manual page from the selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge.
The late-renewal tiers on the renewal page read at least 180 days but not more than five years and five years or more, so a license expired exactly five years falls in both wordings; C reports both tiers as printed and the boundary is flagged [A03] (verify IN-RENEW-D-FIVEYR).
The renewal page ties the points-based knowledge exam to drivers aged 21 or older, while the first chapter's exam list states the six-point trigger without an age; C keeps each statement on its own page [A03].
The SSA card sentence on the amendment page is ambiguous about what is replaced online; it is kept in C2 as printed with a scope note [A04].
Placard fees and the organization-placard expiry rule come from one page and no fee amount is printed, so no amount is stated [A02].
Online service limits, kiosk options, form numbers and the BMV phone line are service details that can change and are isolated as dynamic.

corpus_stability.reason: The Indiana Driver's Manual back cover reads Published July 2026 and tells readers to check IN.gov/BMV for updates; the BMV manual page says printed manuals are updated at most once a year, so the selected pages are treated as stable within a year while fees and service details stay dynamic.

verification_debt.claim_text: Physical page 24 describes one tier as expired at least 180 days but not more than five years and another as expired five years or more, so the testing required for a license expired exactly five years is ambiguous; confirm with the BMV renewal rules before teaching the boundary.
